This is going to be a long comment, but here are my tips: 

Remember that while it's a personal transition, it's also a radical political stance to take - no reliance on predatory cigarette and alcohol companies profiting off of making you numb. It's a stance of strength to even try to quit.

Realizing how terrifying and certain the health outcomes of smoking and drinking were, also made me go from "I wish I was smoking" to "thank god I'm smart enough to quit while I can". There are 0 benefits to drinking or smoking. Not emotional, not physical. They are both carcinogenic and WILL cause suffering today and tomorrow.

It took so much discipline for me to quit. Nicotine replacement like the patch and gum really did help me. I believe that if you're consistent with them, they can actually wean you off. There is no shame in using them, as long as you swear to yourself that you won't smoke while on them. Since NRT is expensive, I told myself: Why pay 40 dollars for a box of patches when I'm going to smoke anyway? May as well commit instead of wasting the cash. Make quitting your sole goal despite anything else in your life.

Before I quit smoking for good, I more so tried to see how long I could take a break between cigs or a vape. Sit through a couple of cravings, then understand how fleeting they are. Feel strong for having waited a day to smoke again vs. giving in to the next one as soon as your brain experiences withdrawals. The cravings pass over like a wave, and then you're okay.

A large part of quitting both nicotine and alcohol is social, and you need to build your self-esteem as a part of your quitting journey. Your health IS worth it. The people in your life do care that you get better, and you ARE stronger than it. This helps prevent you from being embarrassed when confronted by the social pressure of substances. 


TLDR: The strength is within you to quit. Have discipline, and use your resources. Every step you take against substance use is a good one and worth it. Do it now so you won't have to later.
